name: Make a simple basket
blurb: A round willow or rush basket teaches the whole logic of weaving: a rigid framework of spokes and a flexible weaver going over and under.
gear: Soaked willow, rush, or split cane
steps: Soak the material until it bends without cracking — this can take hours for willow and is not optional.
Make the base: cross two sets of thick rods, then bind them with a pairing weave to lock the centre.
Open out the spokes evenly like the spokes of a wheel and continue weaving the flat base.
Upsett: kink each spoke upwards to form the walls, then weave a few rows of a tight waling weave to hold the shape.
Weave the sides with a simple randing or pairing weave, keeping the tension even and the shape symmetrical.
Finish with a border by folding each spoke down and weaving it into the rim.
tips: Dry material cracks. Keep it damp throughout the whole session.
Uneven spoke spacing at the base ruins the shape of everything above it. Get the base right.
proof: A basket that holds its shape, has an even rim, and carries real weight.
